final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest EVEscape signal (z=0.712) at a known N-linked glycosylation site critical for antibody shielding; low PLM plausibility (0.001) reflects model limitations at glycan sites under immune pressure rather than true fitness cost.

stop_reason.detail: All 4 tool calls have been consumed; no further evidence can be gathered for unevaluated candidates.

history.rationale: N279 is in the CD4 binding site loop and is a known glycan/antibody contact; N279K is a well-documented escape mutation from broadly neutralizing antibodies targeting the CD4bs.
Strong escape signal (0.712) but extremely low PLM plausibility (0.001) suggests this mutation may severely compromise folding/replication fitness, reducing overall confidence.
N279K shows strong escape signal (z=0.712) but extremely low PLM plausibility (0.0014), suggesting potential fitness cost. Retaining but noting the tension between escape and replication fitness.
Strong escape signal (z=0.712) but very low PLM plausibility (z=0.001) suggests potential fitness cost. Lowering confidence slightly to reflect this tension.
N301 is a glycan important for 2G12 and some CD4bs bNAbs; removal can confer escape while the position may tolerate substitution.
Moderate escape (0.558) combined with near-zero PLM plausibility (0.000) makes this a poor candidate for retaining replication fitness.

rejection.reason: Moderate escape (0.558) combined with near-zero PLM plausibility (0.000) makes this a poor candidate for retaining replication fitness.

history.rationale: N279K has very low PLM plausibility; N279D is a more conservative substitution at the same glycosylation site that may retain escape while being more structurally tolerated. Position 279 is a known N-linked glycosylation site critical for antibody shielding.
More conservative substitution at the same glycosylation site; no direct evidence yet but hypothesized to balance escape and fitness better than N279K.
N301A had zero PLM plausibility; N301S is a more conservative substitution at the supersite glycan that might retain some escape while being more tolerated.
